newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Guinea Bissau to hold elections in 1998 and 1999.
newsitem.headline: Guinea Bissau to hold elections in 1998 and 1999.

text.p: The West African state of Guinea Bissau will hold municipal elections in 1998 to be followed by presidential and parliamentary elections in 1999, state radio reported on Saturday, quoting the president.
President Joao Bernardo Viera did not specify the dates of the polls in the former Portuguese colony.
Bissau Radio was monitored in nearby Gambia.
Earlier this month, Viera named Carlos Correia as prime minister to replace Manuel Saturnino Costa who was sacked.
The radio said Viera dissolved the government on May 26 because of its failure to resolve Guinea Bissau's economic crisis. Correia was prime minister from 1991 to 1994.
Guinea Bissau became the 15th member of the West Africa CFA franc zone in May, abandoning its peso currency for the CFA franc used by most francophone countries in the region.
